title: Singapore’s DayOne Files for US IPO Joining AI Data Center Rush
source_used: The Straits Times (https://www.straitstimes.com/business/singapores-dayone-files-for-us-ipo-joining-data-centre-rush, carries Bloomberg's article text), The Business Times (prospectus details) and Renaissance Capital. Bloomberg page itself blocked (HTTP 403).
key_facts: DayOne Data Centers, headquartered in Singapore, filed for a US IPO on 5 Oct 2026 (SEC filing) and expects its American depositary receipts to trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol DODC (Bloomberg, via The Straits Times).
For the six months to 30 June 2026 it reported revenue of $512 million (against $151.5 million a year earlier) and a net loss of $81.9 million (against $13.5 million).

It filed confidentially in August; Bloomberg earlier reported the IPO may seek as much as $5 billion at a valuation of about $20 billion; no pricing terms are disclosed in the filing (Renaissance Capital).
The offering is led by Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citigroup.

DayOne was once the international arm of GDS Holdings (GDS International until its 2025 rebrand); it closed a $4.5 billion Series C round in June led by Coatue and Hillhouse, and its backers include SoftBank Vision Fund and Citadel's Ken Griffin.

It runs or is developing data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain, and is part of a wave of data-centre IPOs that includes Switch and Nscale (Bloomberg).

The Business Times, reading the prospectus: 87% of first-half revenue came from Malaysia; the largest customer, an unnamed tech company with a leading short-form video platform, supplied 69.2% of first-half revenue; two existing customers have been designated 'Chinese military companies' by the US Department of War.
quote_evidence: DayOne Data Centers filed for a US initial public offering, setting the Singapore-headquartered firm up to capture investors’ resilient demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The data centre operator had a net loss of US$81.9 million (S$104.8 million) on revenue of US$512 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a net loss of US$13.5 million on revenue of US$151.5 million in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to its filing on Oct 5 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
The prospectus also revealed that two of DayOne’s existing customers have been designated as “Chinese military companies” by the US Department of War.
why_it_matters_hint: A builder of AI data centres is asking public investors for money, with sales more than tripling but losses widening and one customer supplying most of its revenue.
event_date: SEC filing 5 Oct 2026 (US time); Bloomberg report the same day
notes: Bloomberg's page could not be opened; its text was read on The Straits Times (credit BLOOMBERG), with The Business Times and Renaissance Capital for the prospectus details. Bookings figures differ between outlets (1.5 GW in the Bloomberg text, 2.3 GW at The Business Times and Renaissance Capital) and are not used.
